title: The Akal Takht rebuilt
hook: Sikhs pulled down the government-repaired Akal Takht and rebuilt it by volunteer labor

segments.voice: Yesterday, peace returns, and your line was healing, slowly. Were you patient with one wound? Today, a new week opens with a building that had to be torn down before it could heal. Day one thousand sixteen.

A new building stands where a broken one stood. The walls are straight, the paint is fresh, the dome is whole. And the people it was built for won't accept it. They gather with hammers and baskets and take it apart, brick by brick, by hand. Then they start again, from the ground, carrying the new bricks themselves. It sounds like waste. To the Sikhs who did it at the Akal Takht, after June, it was the only way the building could be theirs again. Today's word is the way they did it: kar seva.
screen: `A NEW BUILDING, REFUSED.` → `TAKEN APART BY HAND.` → `KAR SEVA.`

segments.voice: First, the throne. The Akal Takht, the throne of the Timeless One, stands facing the Darbar Sahib in Amritsar, the seat from which Sikh decisions and edicts go out. This path has met it before. In June it was badly damaged in the fighting. Second, the repair. The government had it repaired quickly, with a Nihang leader, Baba Santa Singh, at the head of the work. But to the Sikh bodies that speak for the panth, a throne repaired by the government that had broken it was not a throne. They called it the government's building, and the Akal Takht later censured Santa Singh for his part in it. Third, the rebuilding. Kar seva volunteers pulled the repaired building down and rebuilt the Akal Takht by kar seva. Kar means work; seva means selfless service. Volunteers, led by kar seva teams, carried earth and bricks and mortar on their heads, the way kar seva is done. No wage. No contract. Just hands. That's today's line: built by volunteers. Fourth, the root. At Ang 286 of the Guru Granth Sahib, in the Sukhmani, Guru Arjan says that the one who serves without wanting anything in return reaches the Lord. In Sikh teaching, seva is not a side activity. It is a way the hands pray. And for a throne that stands for the panth's own voice, only the panth's own hands would do.
screen: `THE THRONE OF THE TIMELESS ONE.` · `REPAIRED BY THE GOVERNMENT, REFUSED.` · `PULLED DOWN, REBUILT BY HAND.` · `ANG 286: SERVE, WANTING NOTHING.` · then, large: `BUILT BY VOLUNTEERS.`

segments.voice: Two minutes to plan an hour of seva. Sit, and let your hands rest in your lap. Ask yourself where an hour of your hands could help: a food bank, a cleanup, a gurdwara kitchen, a neighbor's garden, a shelter. Breathe in, and picture yourself arriving. Breathe out, and picture the work: carrying, washing, sweeping, stirring. No one paying you, no one thanking you. Pick one, and pick a day. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you decide. The bell holds the time.
Kar seva. Kar is work, seva is selfless service: volunteer labor that builds and cleans the Gurus' places, and that rebuilt the Akal Takht. Today's word.
Your line: built by volunteers. Today, give one hour of your hands to something that isn't yours, for no pay, and let it be enough. Day one thousand sixteen.

howItsDone: Sikhs remember the rebuilding of the Akal Takht by kar seva as a statement that the panth's throne must be built by the panth itself; kar seva volunteers still build and clean gurdwaras by hand.

trapdoor: what you thought: volunteers helping on a building site.
what it means: selfless work for the Guru's house, which rebuilt the Akal Takht after the government's repair was refused.
what a scholar hears: the refusal was about authority as much as bricks: a throne for the panth's voice had to be built by the panth, not by the state.

notes: New week starts here (days 1016–1022). No dates are given on purpose (claims rule): neither the repair, the demolition nor the completion of the rebuilt Akal Takht is dated.

Please confirm: the government repair with Baba Santa Singh of the Budha Dal; its rejection as a government ('sarkari') building; the Akal Takht's later declaration against Santa Singh (described as 'guilty of a serious breach'; he was declared tankhaiya / excommunicated: confirm which); demolition and rebuilding by kar seva led by kar seva teams (names of the kar seva leaders deliberately left out).
'This path has met it many times' refers to earlier days on the Akal Takht; confirm.
'as Sikhs have done at shrines for generations' is a general claim; tomorrow's day (Building by hand) covers kar seva broadly, so today keeps to the Akal Takht.

Editor pass: Ang 26 (the root on day 1006, ten days earlier) replaced with Ang 286, Sukhmani (sevaa karat hoe nihkaamee tis kau hot paraapat suaamee), paraphrased; please confirm Ang.
